content.value_statement: Image research can require manual searching across regions and languages. This skill runs a BrowserAct workflow to return structured Google Images metadata for a defined query.
actual_capabilities: Submits a keyword query to the BrowserAct Google Images workflow.
Sets supported country and language preferences for a search.
Configures scroll depth and the maximum requested result count.
Polls BrowserAct for task status for up to five minutes.
Prints the API response, including returned image metadata when available.
limitations: Requires a valid BROWSERACT_API_KEY and a BrowserAct account.
Uses BrowserAct and Google Images results, so availability and output depend on those services.
The script does not download images or verify licensing rights.
The current script returns after polling and does not reach its result-retrieval block.

use_cases.title: Research visual search results
use_cases.description: Compare image-search results for a topic across supported regions and languages.

use_cases.title: Find product-style references
use_cases.description: Collect result titles, links, thumbnails, and source names for a product query.

use_cases.title: Plan creative research
use_cases.description: Review structured image-search metadata before selecting sources for a design brief.

prompt_templates.title: Start an image search
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Google Images for "solar garden lights" in the United States and summarize the returned metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Compare two markets
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the same Google Images search for "wireless earbuds" in the United States and Japan. Compare the visible result sources and titles.

prompt_templates.title: Collect product references
prompt_templates.prompt: Search for "minimalist desk lamp" in Germany. Request 30 results and list product-style entries with their click-through links.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a localized research brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Search for "sustainable packaging" in France and Japan. Use the supported language settings and organize returned titles, sources, and thumbnails by market.

output_examples.input: Search for "ceramic coffee mug" in the United Kingdom.
output: Task status updates while BrowserAct processes the request.
A returned list may include titles, source names, links, thumbnail URLs, and result indexes.

output_examples.input: Search for "running shoes" in Japan with 20 results.
output: A localized task request using the Japan country setting.
Returned metadata can be grouped by product-style status and source site.

best_practices: Store BROWSERACT_API_KEY in a secure environment or secret manager.
Use specific keywords and supported country and language codes.
Review source links and image rights before using any discovered content.
anti_patterns: Do not paste API keys into chat prompts or output logs.
Do not assume every returned image is licensed for reuse.
Do not request more results than the research question needs.

faq.question: What credential does this skill need?
faq.answer: It requires a valid BROWSERACT_API_KEY for the BrowserAct workflow.

faq.question: Can it search different countries?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports the country codes listed in the skill documentation.

faq.question: Can it change the search language?
faq.answer: Yes. It accepts the supported Google Images language settings.

faq.question: What information can results include?
faq.answer: Results can include titles, links, source names, logos, thumbnails, product status, and indexes.

faq.question: Does it download image files?
faq.answer: No. The documented output is metadata from the BrowserAct API response.

faq.question: Can I share an API key in chat?
faq.answer: No. Set the key through a secure environment or secret manager instead.
